items.question: How many parents believe that raising children today requires a wider circle of trust than it did a generation ago, according to new research?
items.context: Finding: Seven in 10 parents believe that raising children today requires a wider circle of trust than it did a generation ago, according to new research.
items.talk: When choosing care for a child, what matters most: cost, location, trust or flexibility?

items.question: How many dual-income households say they work out of necessity, highlighting the critical role trusted childcare plays in helping parents participate in the workforce?
items.context: Finding: Nine in ten dual-income households say they work out of necessity, highlighting the critical role trusted childcare plays in helping parents participate in the workforce.
items.talk: When choosing care for a child, what matters most: cost, location, trust or flexibility?

items.question: How many (58%) of Gen Zers say the same – 24% saying they are ‘very’ likely and 34% ‘somewhat’ likely?
items.context: Finding: Nearly 3 in 5 (58%) of Gen Zers say the same – 24% saying they are ‘very’ likely and 34% ‘somewhat’ likely.
items.talk: Does this finding match the way you are spending, saving or giving right now?

items.question: How many U.S. adults (83%) express being at least ‘somewhat’ concerned regarding biometric data collection?
items.context: Finding: More than 4 in 5 U.S. adults (83%) express being at least ‘somewhat’ concerned regarding biometric data collection.
items.talk: Does this number surprise you, or does it sound about right?

items.question: What percentage of Americans say they prefer a human rather than automation to prepare their food at a restaurant?
items.context: Ipsos found the preference for human-prepared restaurant food has grown since 2023.
items.talk: Would you care if a robot prepared your meal as long as it tasted good?

items.question: When ordering fast food, what percentage of Americans say they would rather interact with a person than an automated system?
items.context: Three in four Americans told Ipsos they prefer human interaction when ordering fast food.
items.talk: Do kiosks make ordering faster, or do they turn customers into unpaid cashiers?

items.question: How many (40%) haven’t started booking anything yet?
items.context: Finding: Roughly 2 in 5 (40%) haven’t started booking anything yet.
items.talk: Does this number surprise you, or does it sound about right?

items.question: How many young women get health and wellness information from influencers?
items.context: Finding: Nearly 6 in 10 young women get health and wellness information from influencers
items.talk: Would you trust health advice from an influencer, or do you want it from a medical professional?

items.question: What percentage of U.S. adults say they use AI chatbots to search for information?
items.context: Searching for information was the most commonly reported chatbot use in Pew's 2026 survey.
items.talk: What have you stopped Googling because you now ask AI instead?

items.question: Among employed U.S. adults, what percentage say they use AI chatbots for tasks at work?
items.context: Pew found more than a third of employed adults report using chatbots for work tasks.
items.talk: What work task would you happily hand to AI forever?

items.question: What percentage of Americans said they had canceled a streaming subscription during the previous six months?
items.context: Ipsos reported the share had risen by 10 percentage points from the prior month.
items.talk: If you could keep only one streaming service, which one survives?

items.question: What percentage of Americans agree they can get better discounts online than in stores?
items.context: Ipsos found a strong majority believes online shopping offers better discounts.
items.talk: What do you still refuse to buy online?

items.question: Among adults who made charitable donations, how many gave money to someone they knew personally, donated while checking out at a store, or provided non-financial support to people in their community?
items.context: Finding: About 4 in 10 gave money to someone they knew personally, donated while checking out at a store, or provided non-financial support to people in their community.
items.talk: What type of cause are you most likely to donate to, and what makes you trust an organization enough to give?

items.question: How many volunteered their time to a charitable organization?
items.context: Finding: Three in 10 volunteered their time to a charitable organization.
items.talk: What type of cause are you most likely to donate to, and what makes you trust an organization enough to give?

items.question: How many people say their household has donated to an organization that aids people in the U.S. and 35% gave to a religious institution?
items.context: Finding: About 4 in 10 say their household has donated to an organization that aids people in the U.S. and 35% gave to a religious institution.
items.talk: What type of cause are you most likely to donate to, and what makes you trust an organization enough to give?

items.question: How many people have received assistance from a government program or a family member outside their household?
items.context: Finding: Two in 10 have received assistance from a government program or a family member outside their household.
items.talk: What type of cause are you most likely to donate to, and what makes you trust an organization enough to give?

items.question: How many adults plan to go to bed before midnight on New Year’s Eve this year?
items.context: Finding: About 4 in 10 adults plan to go to bed before midnight on New Year’s Eve this year.
items.talk: Does this finding match the way you are spending, saving or giving right now?

items.question: How many people have put up holiday decorations before Thanksgiving or plan to watch sports on Christmas day?
items.context: Finding: Two in 10 have put up holiday decorations before Thanksgiving or plan to watch sports on Christmas day.
items.talk: Does this finding match the way you are spending, saving or giving right now?

items.question: How many Americans across income levels cite the upfront price as a reason they would not purchase an EV?
items.context: Finding: About 8 in 10 Americans across income levels cite the upfront price as a reason they would not purchase an EV.
items.talk: Does this finding match the way you are spending, saving or giving right now?

items.question: How many sports fans watch a game at least a few times a week?
items.context: Finding: Three in 10 sports fans watch a game at least a few times a week
items.talk: Have streaming services made it easier or harder for you to watch the sports you want?
